newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-COURIER SURVIVES A SCARE AT LIPTON CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-COURIER SURVIVES A SCARE AT LIPTON CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Jim Courier, showing glimpses of the fire that made him number one in the world five years ago, won a tough third-round match at the $4.45 million Lipton Championships on Monday.

Courier, ranked 26th and still struggling to regain the form that won him two Australian and two French Open titles, fought hard from 4-1 down in the third set to defeat talented Australian lefthander Scott Draper 4-6 6-1 6-4.
Thomas Muster of Austria, the second seed, handed 166th-ranked Tommy Haas a lesson on stadium court, defeating the 19-year old German prospect 6-1 6-2 in 52 minutes.
The women's second seed was upset when Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain played a lacklustre match with little-known Sandrine Testud of France, going out 6-0 7-5.
Testud, ranked 29th, missed a match point at 5-4 but the usually tigerish Spaniard could not force a comeback, going out on the second match point with a netted forehand.
Top seeded woman Martina Hingis of Switzerland was tested in her fourth-round match before beating Russia's Elena Likhovtseva 6-3 2-6 6-3.

Hingis will meet Mary Joe Fernandez in the quarter-finals. Fernandez, ranked 12th, beat her former friend and doubles partner Lindsay Davenport 6-2 6-4. Davenport, ranked seventth, dumped Fernandez as her doubles partner at the end of last year, causing a rift between the two.
Monica Seles, the fourth seed, needed just 55 minutes to advance past Asa Carlsson of Sweden 6-2 6-1.
Courier was overwhelmed at first by the booming lefthanded serves and searing groundstrokes of Draper, often compared to his famous lefthanded countryman Rod Laver, but yet to fulfil that potential.

Draper, 22, won the first set 6-4 before going off the boil in the second to drop it 6-1. But the Australian got the first break of serve in the third set, pounding groundstroke winners to run his opponent all over the court.

He led 4-1 before Courier fought back, varying the pace and coming to net, breaking Draper for 4-3. Courier then used an effective serve and volley game to reach 4-4, winning the game with a low, angled drop shot.

As quickly as Courier's confidence returned, Draper's evaporated. An ace saved one break point in the next game, but the Australian handed Courier the lead 5-4 with a double fault. The American served out the match 6-4 as Draper netted a backhand return.

"I picked up my game at 4-2 and cut out the unforced errors which were killing me in the match," said Courier of his late comeback. "Clearly today I didn't play my best tennis, but I used my brain in the end to win the match. That's very satisfying."

Draper said he paid the price for overconfidence. "I felt like the match was mine and that's a big mistake against a guy like Courier. My serve went off and he changed his tactics and went to the net more. It's pretty tough to beat a player like that with your second serve."
